title: Risk of Virological Failure After Switch to a Tenofovir-Sparing Dual Therapy in Virologically Suppressed People With HIV and Past HBV Infection.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to compare the effectiveness of tenofovir-based triple regimens to tenofovir-sparing dual therapies in virologically suppressed people living with HIV and past hepatitis B infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was an emulation of a target trial including adults with HIV and HBsAg-/HBcAb+ serostatus from five University Hospitals, comparing tenofovir-based triple regimens to tenofovir-sparing dual therapies.
analysis.methods: The study estimated the probability of virological failure (defined as HIV-RNA > 50 cp/mL or a single HIV-RNA ≥ 200 cp/mL) through a weighted Kaplan-Meier estimator.
analysis.main_results: In the weighted analysis, the estimated probabilities of virological failure were 29.3% for dual therapy and 29.9% for triple therapy at 5 years (difference: 0.5%; 95% CI: -28.7, +21.6).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that switching to a tenofovir-sparing dual therapy was not associated with an increased risk of virological failure compared to continuing a triple therapy in this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support the use of tenofovir-sparing dual therapies as a viable option for virologically suppressed people with HIV and past HBV infection, potentially reducing long-term tenofovir exposure.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was an emulation of a target trial, which may introduce unmeasured confounding; however, the large sample size and robust statistical methods provide moderate confidence in the results.

analysis.summary_en: This study compared tenofovir-based triple regimens to tenofovir-sparing dual therapies in virologically suppressed people living with HIV and past hepatitis B infection. Among 415 eligible participants, 71 started dual therapy during follow-up. The estimated 5-year probability of virological failure was similar between groups (29.3% for dual therapy vs. 29.9% for triple therapy). A higher virological failure risk was observed in participants with undetectable HBsAb at longest follow-up, but this was independent of treatment group. The findings suggest that switching to tenofovir-sparing dual therapy is not associated with increased virological failure risk in this population.

title: Self-reported hepatitis B vaccination uptake and associated factors among adults in a tertiary hospital, Nasarawa State, Nigeria.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine. In Nigeria, adult vaccination coverage and completion rates are not well characterized within hospital-based populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted among 1,200 adults attending Federal Medical Centre (FMC) Keffi, Nasarawa State, Nigeria. The mean age of respondents was predominantly 36-40 years (32.5%), with males constituting 72.3%, most had tertiary education (91.8%) and were civil servants (83.4%).
analysis.methods: Data on socio-demographics, HBV-related knowledge, attitudes, perceived barriers, vaccination uptake, and completion were collected using a structured questionnaire. Knowledge and attitude scores were categorized into poor, fair, and good levels. Associations between socio-demographic characteristics and vaccination uptake were examined using chi-square and Fisher's exact tests, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.
analysis.main_results: Overall awareness of HBV was high (95.5%), with a mean knowledge score of 12.37 ± 1.42. Good knowledge was observed in 74.2% of respondents, while 57.2% demonstrated good attitudes toward HBV prevention. Vaccination uptake was high, with 93.5% reporting receipt of at least one vaccine dose, but only 22.3% had completed the recommended three-dose schedule.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Despite high HBV vaccination initiation and knowledge levels, substantial gaps in vaccine completion persist. The study highlights that willingness to complete vaccination was reported by 81.6% of respondents, indicating potential for improvement if barriers are addressed.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Addressing financial, informational, and access-related barriers is essential to improve full vaccination coverage among Nigerian adults. These findings can inform targeted interventions to enhance HBV vaccination completion rates in hospital settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in a single tertiary hospital, which may limit generalizability to other populations or settings. Despite the large sample size, the evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential self-reporting bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated hepatitis B vaccination uptake and completion rates among 1,200 adults in a Nigerian tertiary hospital. Despite high awareness (95.5%) and vaccination initiation (93.5%), only 22.3% completed the three-dose schedule. Key barriers included high cost (72.4%), limited access (96.9%), fear of side effects (71.9%), and insufficient information (73.5%). No significant associations were found between socio-demographic factors and vaccination uptake. The findings highlight the need to address financial, access, and informational barriers to improve full vaccination coverage, with 81.6% of respondents willing to complete vaccination if these issues are resolved.

title: Trends in Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV Seroprevalence in the Netherlands: Insights From Two Decades of Nationwide PIENTER Serosurveys.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV), and HIV remain public health challenges despite effective treatments and preventive options, with infections often being asymptomatic and leading to undiagnosed cases and preventable morbidity and mortality.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We estimated HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence, identified determinants, and assessed trends over 20 years using data from 14,444 participants aged 15-79 years from three nationwide cross-sectional serosurveys (PIENTER: 1995-1996, 2006-2007, and 2016-2017) in the Netherlands.
analysis.methods: Participants completed questionnaires on demographics, behaviour, and socio-economic factors, and serum samples were tested for HBV and HCV in all rounds and HIV in 2017; seroprevalence estimates were weighted to the Dutch population, trends were analysed using weighted Poisson regression, and determinants were evaluated using multivariable Poisson regression.
analysis.main_results: Weighted HBV seroprevalence remained stable across surveys (3%-5% past or present infection; < 0.4% active infection), with highest prevalence among first-generation migrants, older age, migration background, and STI history as key determinants; only 9% of active HBV cases were aware of their status.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence remain low in the Netherlands but are concentrated in specific groups with limited awareness, highlighting the importance of continued population-based monitoring to guide public health policy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted prevention, screening, and linkage-to-care strategies to achieve the 2030 WHO elimination goals, emphasizing the need for focused interventions in high-risk populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and potential underreporting of asymptomatic cases, though the large sample size and nationwide scope enhance reliability.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed trends in HBV, HCV, and HIV seroprevalence in the Netherlands over two decades using three nationwide serosurveys (1995-1996, 2006-2007, 2016-2017) with 14,444 participants. HBV seroprevalence remained stable at 3%-5% for past or present infection and <0.4% for active infection, with highest rates among first-generation migrants. Only 9% of active HBV cases were aware of their status. The findings underscore the need for targeted screening and prevention strategies in high-risk groups to achieve WHO elimination goals, while highlighting the importance of continued population-based monitoring.

title: Differential Hepatitis B Surface Antigen Glycan Isomer Kinetics Between Tenofovir Alafenamide and Entecavir: Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk Stratification in Hepatitis B e Antigen‐Positive Patients

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study was needed because nucleos(t)ide analog therapy suppresses hepatitis B virus DNA but residual hepatocellular carcinoma risk persists, and O-glycosylated hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer uniquely reflects virion burden.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study evaluated the impact of tenofovir alafenamide versus entecavir on 48-week HBsAgGi kinetics and its utility in stratifying HCC risk in 90 NA-naïve patients (ETV: 73; TAF: 17).
analysis.methods: A favourable response was defined as a reduction or maintenance of low HBsAgGi levels, and penalised odds ratio was used to compare treatment effects.
analysis.main_results: TAF independently predicted a favourable response compared with ETV (penalised odds ratio 3.60, p = 0.030), and in HBeAg-positive patients, a poor response was associated with increased HCC risk (hazard ratio 7.34, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.96–20.35, p = 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that on-treatment HBsAgGi response is a specific surrogate marker for stratifying residual HCC risk in HBeAg-positive patients, and TAF is more effective than ETV in inducing these favourable kinetics.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Adding HBsAgGi response to the aMAP score improved long-term HCC prediction exclusively in the HBeAg-positive cohort, providing a tool for risk stratification.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The assay targets genotype C-specific O-glycosylation, so findings cannot be generalised to genotypes A, B, or D; evidence strength is moderate due to limited sample size and wide confidence intervals.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated differential hepatitis B surface antigen glycan isomer kinetics between tenofovir alafenamide and entecavir in 90 NA-naïve patients to stratify hepatocellular carcinoma risk. TAF independently predicted a favourable HBsAgGi response compared to ETV, with a significant interaction between HBeAg status and HBsAgGi response in HCC development. In HBeAg-positive patients, poor response correlated with increased HCC risk (HR 7.34), and adding HBsAgGi to the aMAP score improved prediction. However, findings are limited to genotype C due to assay specificity, and evidence strength is moderate due to sample size and wide confidence intervals.

title: Factors Associated With Surface Antigen (HBsAg) Clearance in a Spanish Cohort of Chronic Hepatitis B Patients: Influence on the Long-Term Prognosis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to identify factors contributing to hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) clearance in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) infection and determine the influence of clearance on long-term prognosis in a Spanish cohort.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective open cohort study of 453 patients with CHB infection was recruited in the Liver Unit of the Internal Department of two hospitals in Málaga (Spain) between 1991 and 2022, with follow-up ranging from 0.5 to 36.08 years.
analysis.methods: Multivariate Cox regression analysis was conducted to identify factors associated with HBsAg clearance, and the impact of clearance on long-term prognosis was evaluated using a combined prognostic endpoint: need for liver transplantation, liver complications, or liver-related mortality. Time-to-event curves were constructed using the Kaplan-Meir method, with comparisons via log-rank test.
analysis.main_results: During follow-up, 96/453 patients (21.2%) lost surface antigen (1.96/100 patients per year). Independent factors associated with HBsAg clearance included age over 40 years at first assessment (HR 2.21), baseline DNA HBV below 3.3 log10 (HR 3.44), and loss of HBeAg during follow-up (HR 7.23).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted HBsAg clearance as associated with a better long-term hepatic prognosis, highlighting the significance of age, viral load, and HBeAg seroconversion as key predictors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform surveillance and management strategies for CHB patients, emphasizing the importance of monitoring older patients, those with low viral load, and HBeAg seroconversion to improve long-term outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence strength is moderate, limited by its observational design and potential confounding factors, though the large sample size and long follow-up enhance reliability.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective cohort study in Spain investigated factors associated with HBsAg clearance in 453 chronic hepatitis B patients over 31 years. Key findings included a 21.2% clearance rate (1.96/100 patient-years), with older age (>40 years), low baseline viral load (<2000 IU/mL), and HBeAg loss as independent predictors. Clearance was linked to improved long-term prognosis, reducing liver-related complications, transplantation needs, and mortality. The study provides valuable insights for CHB management, highlighting the importance of these factors in predicting favorable outcomes.

title: Absence of Detectable Anti‐ HDV Antibodies Among HBsAg ‐Positive Blood Donors, HIV ‐Infected Individuals and Patients With Chronic Hepatitis B in Sao Paulo, Brazil: Evaluation Using a Rapid Lateral Flow Assay

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) infection in HBV‐infected individuals is associated with severe clinical outcomes, and screening is recommended in HBsAg‐positive patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a retrospective cross‐sectional study to assess anti‐HDV antibodies among 46 HBsAg‐positive blood donors at Fundação Pró‐Sangue/Hemocentro de São Paulo, 381 patients with chronic hepatitis B from the Central Laboratory Division of HC‐FMUSP, and 189 individuals from the Hepatology Clinic of HC‐FMUSP (101 HIV‐infected and 88 chronically HBV‐infected).
analysis.methods: We used a rapid lateral flow assay (LFA) to assess anti‐HDV antibodies in Brazil, where HDV is highly endemic in the North, while data from the Southeast, particularly São Paulo, remain limited. Anti‐HDV antibodies were detected using a validated LFA. Positive controls (n = 24) included samples previously confirmed by ELISA and/or PCR, predominantly infected with HDV genotypes 3 and 8.
analysis.main_results: Among 443,400 blood donations, 48 (0.01%) were positive for at least two HBV markers; of these, 46 were tested for HDV, and all were anti‐HDV negative. All 381 patients undergoing HBV viral load monitoring were anti‐HDV negative, as were all 189 patients receiving hepatology care, including those with HIV coinfection or advanced liver disease.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The absence of detectable anti‐HDV among diverse at‐risk populations in São Paulo is consistent with the low endemicity of HDV infection in southeastern Brazil. These findings, together with the assay's high specificity in HDV RNA‐positive controls, support its potential utility as a screening tool for HDV infection in low‐prevalence settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides valuable data on HDV prevalence in a low-endemicity region, supporting the use of rapid lateral flow assays for HDV screening in such settings. This can inform public health strategies for HDV surveillance and prevention in HBV-infected populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was retrospective and cross-sectional, limiting causal inference. However, the large sample size and validated assay with high specificity in controls provide moderate confidence in the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the prevalence of Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) infection in São Paulo, Brazil, using a rapid lateral flow assay (LFA) among HBsAg-positive blood donors, chronic hepatitis B patients, and HIV-infected individuals. The retrospective cross-sectional study included 46 blood donors, 381 chronic hepatitis B patients, and 189 hepatology clinic patients (101 HIV-infected and 88 HBV-infected). All tested samples were anti-HDV negative, consistent with low HDV endemicity in southeastern Brazil. The LFA showed high specificity in HDV RNA-positive controls, supporting its utility as a screening tool in low-prevalence settings. The findings provide valuable data for public health HDV surveillance strategies.

title: The relationship between mutations in reverse transcriptase region of hepatitis B virus and progression of liver disease

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection progresses to severe liver diseases such as hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet the virological drivers of progression remain incompletely understood. The study aimed to determine whether mutations in the HBV reverse transcriptase (RT) region are associated with the progression of liver disease in Chinese patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study sequenced HBV RT regions from serum samples of 384 Chinese patients with chronic HBV infection, stratified into four clinical groups: 100 asymptomatic carriers (ASC), 101 with chronic hepatitis B, 96 with liver cirrhosis, and 87 with HCC.
analysis.methods: HBV RT regions were amplified and sequenced, with genotyping and amino acid substitutions analyzed using an online HBV genotyping tool and MEGA7.0 software. Logistic regression models were applied to assess associations between RT mutations and advanced liver disease (ALD), including HCC.
analysis.main_results: The mutation rate in the RT region increased progressively from ASC to HCC (P for trend < 0.05). Logistic regression identified rtS106A/C as significantly associated with ALD, while multivariate analysis confirmed rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E as independent risk factors for HBV-related HCC.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that specific RT mutations may serve as predictive biomarkers for disease progression in HBV-infected patients. The study highlights novel associations between rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E and HCC risk, suggesting potential utility in risk stratification.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results cautiously suggest that monitoring RT mutations, particularly rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E, could inform surveillance strategies and early intervention for patients at high risk of developing HCC. The findings may also guide future research into therapeutic targets within the RT region.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design limits causal inference, and the study was conducted in a single region with a specific patient population, which may affect generalizability. The evidence strength is moderate due to potential unmeasured confounders and the absence of longitudinal follow-up.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated whether mutations in the HBV reverse transcriptase (RT) region are linked to liver disease progression in 384 Chinese patients with chronic HBV infection. Sequencing of RT regions revealed a progressive increase in mutation rates from asymptomatic carriers to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. Logistic regression identified rtS106A/C as associated with advanced liver disease, while multivariate analysis confirmed rtH55R/Q/K and rtS137T/Q/E as independent risk factors for HBV-related HCC. The authors propose that these mutations could serve as predictive biomarkers for high-risk patients, potentially informing surveillance and early intervention strategies. However, the cross-sectional design and single-region sampling limit causal conclusions and generalizability, warranting cautious interpretation.

title: HBV PreS/S gene mutations in patients with chronic hepatitis B

analysis.research_question_and_background: Variants in the hepatitis B virus (HBV) PreS/S gene have been suggested to contribute to the development of progressive liver disease. This study aimed to evaluate the association between HBV PreS/S variations and liver histopathology in patients with chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 109 patients under clinical follow-up for chronic hepatitis B were included. Patients with PreS2 mutations had higher fibrosis scores (p < 0.05).
analysis.methods: The HBV PreS/S gene was amplified by PCR and sequenced using the Sanger method. Amino acid substitutions, nonsense mutations, and deletions were analyzed in relation to liver fibrosis stage.
analysis.main_results: Overall, 58 of 389 amino acid sites (14.9%) in the HBV PreS/S gene showed substitutions, with the highest mutation rate observed in the PreS2 region (27.27%). Mutations L54P (PreS1), F130L/S (PreS2), and S207R/N/I/T and I208T (S gene) were significantly more frequent in patients with advanced fibrosis (F ≥ 3) (p < 0.05). Multivariable analysis identified S207R/N/I/T as an independent risk factor for liver fibrosis.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The S207R/N/I/T mutation in the C-terminal region of the HBV S protein is independently associated with liver fibrosis, while PreS2 mutations may contribute to fibrosis progression in chronic hepatitis B.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that specific HBV PreS/S mutations may serve as biomarkers for advanced liver fibrosis, potentially aiding in risk stratification and monitoring of chronic hepatitis B patients.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study included a relatively small sample size of 109 patients, which may limit the generalizability of the findings. However, the use of multivariable analysis strengthens the evidence for the independent association of S207R/N/I/T mutations with liver fibrosis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the association between HBV PreS/S gene mutations and liver fibrosis in 109 chronic hepatitis B patients. The HBV PreS/S gene was sequenced, revealing that 14.9% of amino acid sites showed substitutions, with the highest mutation rate in the PreS2 region (27.27%). Specific mutations, including L54P, F130L/S, S207R/N/I/T, and I208T, were significantly more frequent in patients with advanced fibrosis (F ≥ 3). Multivariable analysis identified S207R/N/I/T as an independent risk factor for liver fibrosis. The findings suggest that these mutations may serve as biomarkers for advanced liver disease, potentially aiding in clinical management and risk assessment of chronic hepatitis B patients.

title: METTL14 Downregulation Accelerates HBV‐Related Cirrhosis and Hepatocellular Carcinoma by Promoting Type I Interferon Release via the cGAS–STING Pathway Through m 6 A Modification

analysis.research_question_and_background: The pathogenesis of Hepatitis B virus (HBV)-related cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) has not been fully elucidated at present. While METTL14 is crucial in innate immunity, its specific role in HBV-related liver disease progression is unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Mouse models of HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC were established to evaluate liver injury, fibrosis, and tumorigenesis. We analyzed METTL14 expression in patient tissues and bioinformatics datasets.
analysis.methods: Mechanistic studies utilized MeRIPqPCR, RIP, and Actinomycin D assays, and hepatocyte-stellate cell co-cultures to investigate METTL14's impact on cGAS mRNA stability, the cGAS-STING pathway, and IFNB1 secretion.
analysis.main_results: METTL14 was downregulated in HBV infection, cirrhosis, and HCC. METTL14 knockdown aggravated liver injury, fibrosis, and tumor formation in mice. Mechanistic studies revealed that METTL14 overexpression in HBV-infected hepatocytes promoted the degradation of cGAS mRNA by increasing its m6A modification, thereby suppressing the cGAS-STING pathway activation and IFNB1 release.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Downregulation of METTL14 reduces the degradation of cGAS mRNA through m6A modification, facilitates the cGAS-STING pathway activation and IFNB1 release, thereby accelerating HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC progressions. Consequently, METTL14 overexpression inhibited stellate cell activation, which was reversed by cGAS-STING agonists.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the METTL14-mediated m6A modification of cGAS mRNA could be a novel therapeutic strategy to prevent or treat HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC by modulating the cGAS-STING pathway and type I interferon release.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study primarily used mouse models and in vitro assays, which may not fully recapitulate human disease complexity. The evidence strength is moderate due to the mechanistic insights but limited by the lack of human interventional data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of METTL14 in HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC, revealing that METTL14 downregulation accelerates disease progression by promoting type I interferon release via the cGAS-STING pathway through m6A modification. The researchers analyzed METTL14 expression in patient tissues and bioinformatics datasets, established mouse models of HBV-related cirrhosis and HCC, and conducted mechanistic studies using MeRIPqPCR, RIP, and Actinomycin D assays. They found that METTL14 overexpression suppresses the cGAS-STING pathway and IFNB1 release, inhibiting stellate cell activation, while METTL14 knockdown aggravates liver injury, fibrosis, and tumor formation. These findings suggest that targeting METTL14-mediated m6A modification could be a novel therapeutic strategy for HBV-related liver diseases.

title: Chronic hepatitis B in a large private hospital network in Türkiye: Clinical characteristics and electronic health record-data gaps

analysis.research_question_and_background: Türkiye has intermediate hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection prevalence and an additional burden of hepatitis D virus (HDV). The study aimed to characterize the clinical features of chronic HBV infection and assess the completeness of electronic health record (EHR) data for HBV monitoring and surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, cross-sectional study using electronic health record (EHR) data from a multicenter private hospital network was conducted, including 18,284 adult patients with chronic HBV infection between 2017 and 2025. The primary analysis included 17,927 adults with HBV monoinfection, defined as patients without a recorded ICD-10 B18.0 diagnosis code for chronic HBV with delta agent.
analysis.methods: The study used EHR data from a multicenter private hospital network to analyze demographic and clinical characteristics, liver disease outcomes, and the availability and consistency of key EHR variables relevant to HBV care, including ALT, HBV DNA, HBeAg, anti-HDV testing, B18.0 diagnosis coding, and structured treatment documentation.
analysis.main_results: Among adult patients with HBV monoinfection, 60.6% were male and the mean age was 53.5 years (SD 14.5). Cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) were recorded in 11.1% and 3.4% of patients, respectively, and were more common among men and older adults. Baseline ALT values were available for 45.5% of HBV monoinfected patients. Among patients without cirrhosis, HCC, or liver failure, both HBV DNA and HBeAg status were available for 1274 of 15,243 patients. Documented anti-HDV testing was available for 2213 of 18,284 patients (12.1%), while 357 patients (2.0%) had recorded B18.0 diagnosis code; only 76 of these 357 patients also had documented anti-HDV testing in available EHR field.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that cirrhosis and HCC were common in this large private-sector EHR cohort of adults with recorded chronic HBV infection, particularly among older adults and men. The study highlights gaps in laboratory monitoring, HDV documentation, and treatment data needed to support HBV surveillance and elimination efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings demonstrate the value of private-sector EHR data for characterizing diagnosed HBV care and highlight the need for improved laboratory monitoring, HDV documentation, and treatment data to support HBV surveillance and elimination efforts.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a private-sector EHR cohort and does not represent national HBV prevalence estimates. The evidence strength is moderate, as the findings are based on retrospective data and highlight gaps in data completeness rather than providing definitive conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the clinical characteristics and electronic health record (EHR) data gaps of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in a large private hospital network in Türkiye. It found that cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) were common, particularly among older adults and men. Baseline ALT values were available for only 45.5% of patients, and HBV DNA and HBeAg status were documented in 8.3% of those without cirrhosis, HCC, or liver failure. Anti-HDV testing was available for 12.1% of patients, while only 2.0% had a recorded B18.0 diagnosis code for HBV with delta agent. The study highlights the importance of private-sector EHR data for HBV care but also identifies significant gaps in laboratory monitoring, HDV documentation, and treatment data. These findings suggest the need for improved data collection and integration to support HBV surveillance and elimination efforts.

title: The Silent Burden of Hepatitis B-Related Stigma.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection is associated with stigma that can lead to negative self-perceptions, social isolation, discrimination, and reduced healthcare engagement. The study sought to elucidate the patient perspective of HBV-related stigma and to construct a patient-centric conceptual model of this experience.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This qualitative study recruited 28 adults with confirmed chronic HBV infection from the US (n=11), China (n=11), and Poland (n=6) through purposive sampling. Semi-structured interviews of approximately 60 minutes were conducted to explore stigma experiences.
analysis.methods: Qualitative interviews were analyzed using Thematic Analysis to categorize stigma concepts into domains and pre-determined stigma types. A patient-centric conceptual model was developed to organize the identified stigma domains.
analysis.main_results: Internalized stigma was reported by all 28 participants (100%), social stigma by 22 participants (79%), and institutional stigma by 16 participants (57%). Seven domains were identified, with social functioning (100%), emotional wellbeing (96%), and HBV transmission (96%) most frequently reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that HBV-related stigma is highly pervasive and inter-related, with internalized stigma being the most common and bothersome, suggesting targeted interventions should prioritize reducing internalized stigma to improve health-related quality of life.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for stigma-reduction strategies in HBV care, particularly addressing internalized stigma, to improve patient engagement with healthcare and overall quality of life across diverse global settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The small sample size (n=28) and qualitative design limit generalizability, and the study did not include participants from regions beyond the US, China, and Poland, which may restrict the conceptual model's applicability to other populations. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study explored the patient experience of stigma associated with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection through semi-structured interviews with 28 adults from the US, China, and Poland. All participants reported internalized stigma, 79% reported social stigma, and 57% reported institutional stigma. Seven stigma-related domains were identified, with social functioning, emotional wellbeing, and HBV transmission most frequently reported. The authors conclude that HBV-related stigma is pervasive and inter-related, with internalized stigma being the most common and bothersome, and recommend prioritizing interventions to reduce internalized stigma to improve health-related quality of life and healthcare engagement.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices Toward Hepatitis B Virus Among Transfusion‐Dependent Thalassemia Patients in Jordan

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study was needed to address the knowledge gap regarding hepatitis B virus awareness and behaviors among transfusion-dependent thalassemia patients in Jordan, a high-risk group due to frequent blood product exposure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 407 transfusion-dependent patients attending hematology clinics in governmental hospitals in Jordan.
analysis.methods: A validated questionnaire assessed socio-demographic data and knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding HBV, with scores classified as good, positive, or safe if ≥75% correct; statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and logistic regression.
analysis.main_results: Of the 407 participants, 114 (28%) had good knowledge, 170 (41.8%) had positive attitudes, and 156 (38.3%) demonstrated safe practices toward HBV; key predictors of good knowledge included older age (AOR 3.81, 95% CI 2.09–6.94) and higher education (AOR 3.05, 95% CI 1.80–5.16).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating suboptimal HBV knowledge, attitudes, and practices among this high-risk group, highlighting the need for targeted interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the need for targeted health education programs and HBV vaccination campaigns for transfusion-dependent patients in Jordan to improve prevention and control.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's cross-sectional design limits causal inference, but the large sample size and validated questionnaire provide moderate evidence strength for assessing KAP associations.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) toward hepatitis B virus (HBV) among 407 transfusion-dependent thalassemia patients in Jordan. Results showed suboptimal KAP, with only 28% having good knowledge, 41.8% positive attitudes, and 38.3% safe practices. Older age and higher education were significant predictors of good knowledge. title: Hepatitis Prevalence Among Key Populations in Nigeria: A Scoping Review

analysis.scope_and_question: This scoping review examines hepatitis B virus (HBV) prevalence among key populations (KPs) in Nigeria, including sex workers, men who have sex with men (MSM), transgender people, people who inject drugs (PWIDs), and people in prisons, to assess the burden and identify knowledge gaps.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A scoping review was conducted following the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, searching six databases and gray literature from 2008–2025. Two independent reviewers screened 1,270 records, included 25 studies covering five KP groups in 12 Nigerian states, and assessed study quality using adapted Joanna Briggs Institute criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: HBV prevalence varied significantly among KPs, ranging from 4.0% in sex workers (Enugu) to 23.0% in prisons, with MSM and transgender people showing 10.0% in Abuja and Lagos. PWIDs recorded 6.6–7.8% HBV prevalence. KPs, particularly prisoners, face a higher hepatitis burden than the general population.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Major evidence gaps exist in Northern Nigeria, HCV research (32% of studies), transgender populations (12%), and rural groups (8%). Methodological weaknesses were found in 68% of studies, limiting the reliability of findings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is an urgent need for more research on HCV, transgender populations, and rural areas, alongside expanded surveillance and integrated HIV-hepatitis services to address the disproportionate burden among KPs in Nigeria.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review assesses HBV prevalence among key populations in Nigeria, finding significant variation (4.0–23.0%) with prisons showing the highest burden. Major gaps exist in HCV research, transgender populations, and rural areas, with 68% of studies having methodological weaknesses. The review calls for expanded surveillance, integrated HIV-hepatitis services, and targeted research to address disparities in northern Nigeria and understudied groups.

title: Diagnostic capacity and utilization of Hepatitis B and C testing across multiple health care sectors in Vietnam

analysis.research_question_and_background: The WHO aims to eliminate hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) as public health threats by 2030, yet diagnosis remains suboptimal in many low- and middle-income countries. Access to diagnostics is often emphasized, but how far existing capacity is used is poorly characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a cross-sectional inventory and utilization audit of serologic (HBsAg, anti-HCV) and molecular (HBV DNA, HCV RNA) testing during 2018–2020 at a private diagnostic network, a public district hospital, and a teaching/research institute in Vietnam.
analysis.methods: Utilization was calculated as tests performed divided by maximum theoretical capacity, and facility-level data on fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) at diagnosis were drawn from routine records.
analysis.main_results: In 2019 (pre-COVID-19 reference year), serologic and PCR utilization were 50.0% and 18.8% at the private network, 5.0% and 21.3% at the public hospital, and lowest at the teaching institute (3.5% and 3.0%). Advanced fibrosis (≥ F3) rose over 2018–2020 from 11.4% to 16.6% in HBV and 21.6% to 37.5% in HCV.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Substantial HBV/HCV diagnostic infrastructure exists in Vietnam but is unevenly used. Most HCC occurred in individuals with HBV infection (52.3% and 21.4% at the two larger sites) and coexisted with high unused capacity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Optimizing use of existing platforms may help address systemic inefficiencies and support elimination efforts. The findings highlight the need to improve utilization of diagnostic capacity to reduce advanced liver disease.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Because data were facility-aggregated, these are associations, not patient-level causal relationships. The evidence strength is moderate due to the cross-sectional design and lack of testing accuracy assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated diagnostic capacity and utilization for hepatitis B and C across three Vietnamese healthcare facilities. The WHO aims to eliminate HBV and HCV by 2030, but diagnosis remains suboptimal in many low- and middle-income countries. Researchers conducted a cross-sectional audit of serologic and molecular testing from 2018-2020, finding substantial but unevenly used diagnostic infrastructure. In 2019, utilization rates varied widely: 50.0% serologic and 18.8% PCR at the private network, compared to 5.0% and 21.3% at the public hospital, and 3.5% and 3.0% at the teaching institute. Advanced fibrosis increased over time, and most HCC cases occurred in HBV-infected individuals despite high unused capacity. The study suggests optimizing existing platforms could address inefficiencies and support elimination efforts, though facility-aggregated data limit causal inferences.

title: The Use of Forward Chaining for Early Detection of Hepatitis B Risk Among Pregnant Women at Beber Community Health Center, Cirebon Regency

analysis.research_question_and_background: Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major public health problem in Indonesia, particularly among pregnant women, where delayed detection may increase the risk of mother-to-child transmission as well as serious complications such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mixed-methods approach with a Research and Development (R&D) design was employed to develop and evaluate the system.
analysis.methods: This study aimed to design a web-based early detection system for hepatitis B in pregnant women using the Forward Chaining method.
analysis.main_results: The developed system was tested on 30 respondents and achieved a 100% success rate in black-box testing. Validation results showed a sensitivity of 100%, specificity of 90%, positive predictive value (PPV) of 82%, negative predictive value (NPV) of 100%, and an accuracy of 93%, indicating good diagnostic performance.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The developed system can assist in the early detection of hepatitis B among pregnant women and may support earlier identification of the risk of mother-to-child transmission in primary healthcare settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The system may help address the high cost of laboratory testing that contributes to delays in diagnosis and treatment, potentially improving early intervention for HBV in pregnant women.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted with a small sample size of 30 respondents, which may limit generalizability. However, the high diagnostic performance metrics suggest moderate evidence strength for the system's effectiveness in this specific setting.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a web-based early detection system for hepatitis B in pregnant women using the Forward Chaining method. Employing a mixed-methods R&D design, the system was tested on 30 respondents, achieving 100% success in black-box testing and showing excellent diagnostic performance with 100% sensitivity, 90% specificity, 82% PPV, 100% NPV, and 93% accuracy. The system addresses the high cost of laboratory testing that contributes to delayed diagnosis, potentially enabling earlier detection of HBV and reducing mother-to-child transmission risks in primary healthcare settings. While the small sample size limits generalizability, the strong performance metrics suggest the system could be a valuable tool for early HBV detection in pregnant women.
